data.title: A randomized controlled trial to establish effects of short-term rapamycin treatment in 24 middle-aged companion dogs
data.authors: Urfer SR; Kaeberlein M et al.

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: A short 10-week course of low-dose rapamycin in healthy pet dogs caused no clinical side effects, and echocardiography suggested improved measures of heart function.
data.abstract_excerpt: Age is the single greatest risk factor for most causes of morbidity and mortality in humans and their companion animals. As opposed to other model organisms used to study aging, dogs share the human environment, are subject to similar risk factors, receive comparable medical care, and develop many of the same age-related diseases humans do. In this study, 24 middle-aged healthy dogs received either placebo or a non-immunosuppressive dose of rapamycin for 10 weeks.

extracted_findings.effect: Short-term rapamycin was well tolerated in middle-aged dogs, with signs of improved cardiac function
